# Calibration as an Inverse Problem

## From the model to the data

::: {.corner-note}
Reductions illustrative
:::

```{python}
plots.forward_map_schematic();
```

$$
\mathcal G_k(\theta) = \mathcal H_k\big(\mathcal M(\theta)\big),
\qquad k \in \{\text{NEE},\ \text{LAI},\ \text{biomass},\ \text{soil C}\}
$$

## Parameters

$\theta$: flux-function parameters and initial pools

. . .

- **Photosynthesis:** capacity, temperature optimum, light response
- **Respiration:** rates, temperature sensitivity
- **Allocation** of new carbon: leaf, wood, roots
- **Phenology:** timing and size of leaf-on
- **Soil water:** holding capacity
- **Initial pools:** wood, soil carbon

. . .

Not measurable at the model's scale $\Rightarrow$ a prior $\pi_0(\theta)$:
plant traits, literature, initial-condition ensemble

## The inverse problem

::: {.model-box .data-box}
[Data model]{.box-title}

$$
y \mid \theta, \Sigma \sim \mathcal N\big(\mathcal G(\theta),\ \Sigma\big),
\qquad
\Sigma = \operatorname{blockdiag}\big(s_1^2 \Sigma_1, \dots, s_K^2 \Sigma_K\big)
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.model-box .prior-box}
[Prior model]{.box-title}

$$
\theta \sim \mathcal N(m, C)
$$

[$\pi_0$: this prior, on the unconstrained (log, logit) scale]{.box-note}
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.model-box .hyper-box}
[Hyperparameter model]{.box-title}

$$
s_k^2 \overset{\text{ind}}{\sim} \mathrm{IG}(a_k, b_k)
$$

[unknown scale of each data type's noise; prior median 1]{.box-note}
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.model-box .posterior-box}
[Posterior]{.box-title}

$$
\pi(\theta, s \mid y) \;\propto\;
\mathcal N\big(y \mid \mathcal G(\theta),\ \Sigma\big)\;
\mathcal N(\theta \mid m, C) \prod_k \mathrm{IG}(s_k^2 \mid a_k, b_k)
$$
:::
:::

## Challenges and responses

::: {.pair-head}
[Challenge]{} [Response]{}
:::

::: {.fragment .pair-row}
[**Expensive $\mathcal G$:** a multi-year simulation, repeated at every
site]{} [**Ensemble methods:** few sequential rounds, each a large batch of
runs in parallel]{}
:::

::: {.fragment .pair-row}
[**No gradients:** compiled code, no adjoint; finite differences cost
$D + 1$ runs]{} [**Derivative-free updates:** ensemble Kalman steps;
random-walk and independence proposals]{}
:::

::: {.fragment .pair-row}
[**Nonsmooth $\mathcal G$:** thresholds (e.g. leaf-on) make it
piecewise]{} [**Global, not local:** ensemble moments rather than
linearization]{}
:::

::: {.fragment .pair-row}
[**The data overwhelm the prior** in a single update]{} [**Tempering:**
$\beta: 0 \to 1$ in adaptive increments]{}
:::

::: {.fragment .pair-row}
[**Ensemble Kalman is approximate** for nonlinear $\mathcal G$]{}
[**Correct it:** importance sampling, SMC or MCMC, seeded by the
ensemble]{}
:::

# Harvard Forest: the likelihood

## Observation operators {.big-table}

::: {.corner-note}
$\mathcal M(\theta)$: the simulated trajectory, three-hourly steps $t$;
units converted to the observations'
:::

Each data type: a reduction of the trajectory $\mathcal M(\theta)$

. . .

| $k$ | $\mathcal H_k(\mathcal M)$ | reduction |
|---|---|---|
| NEE | $\operatorname{mean}_{t \in W} \mathrm{NEE}_t$ | time average over a 12-hour window $W$ |
| LAI | $C^{\text{leaf}}_{t_i} / \lambda$ | leaf carbon at the composite's date |
| Biomass | $\operatorname{mean}_{t \in \text{year } j} C^{\text{wood}}_t / 0.48$ | yearly mean of wood carbon |
| Soil carbon | $\operatorname{mean}_{t} C^{\text{soil}}_t$ | mean over the run |

. . .

$\lambda$: leaf carbon per area (a fixed parameter); 0.48: carbon fraction
of wood

## The noise model

$$
\Sigma_k \;=\; \underbrace{\Sigma^{\text{obs}}_k}_{\text{measurement}} \;+\; \underbrace{\Sigma^{\delta}_k}_{\text{model discrepancy}}
$$

. . .

- **Measurement:** each data product's own reported uncertainty
- **Discrepancy:** what SIPNET gets wrong: structure, drivers, a tower's
  footprint vs the model's pixel

. . .

- Independent across data types
- Scales $s_k$ on NEE night, NEE day, LAI; $s_k^2 = 1$ for biomass and soil
  carbon (too few data)

## NEE: the error is discrepancy {.big-table}

::: {.corner-note}
µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; measurement error in the appendix
:::

| | night | day |
|---|---|---|
| tower's own measurement error (median) | 0.7 | 1.0 |
| residual size, first calibration | 1.6 | 3.2 |

. . .

Discrepancy: a Gaussian process in time,

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\delta_W, \delta_{W'}) = v^\delta\, \rho(t_W - t_{W'}),
\qquad \rho(0) = 1
$$

- $v^\delta$: the size at one window, **fixed**
- $\rho$: the error's **memory**, which the three error models differ in

## Three NEE error models

::: {.fragment}
::: {.model-box .data-box}
[Short memory]{.box-title}

[Errors persist **a day or two**: weather-scale]{}
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.model-box .prior-box}
[Long memory]{.box-title}

[\+ anomalies persisting **a season**: a wet spring, an early leaf-out]{}
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.model-box .hyper-box}
[Recurring bias]{.box-title}

[\+ a bias tied to the **calendar date**: wrong in mid-June $\Rightarrow$
wrong in mid-June every year]{}
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
s_k^2\, \Sigma_k = s_k^2 \Big(\Sigma^{\text{obs}}_k + v^\delta_k\, P_k\Big),
\qquad
(P_k)_{WW'} = \rho_k(t_W - t_{W'})
$$

$$
\rho_k(\Delta) =
\underbrace{w_1\, e^{-|\Delta|/\tau_1}}_{\text{short}}
+ \underbrace{w_2\, e^{-|\Delta|/\tau_2}}_{\text{long}}
+ \underbrace{w_3\, \exp\!\Big(-\frac{2 \sin^2(\pi \Delta / 1\,\text{yr})}{\lambda^2}\Big)}_{\text{recurring}},
\qquad w_1 + w_2 + w_3 = 1
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
- Weights sum to 1: same per-window variance $v^\delta_k$, **different memory**
- Adding a term moves variance from short to long memory; it adds none
:::

## The error models in numbers {.nowrap-table}

::: {.corner-note}
Timescale: where a term's correlation falls to $e^{-1} \approx 0.37$;
recurring: that distance from the same date in another year. Percentages:
the weights. Fitted by maximum likelihood to an earlier calibration's
residuals
:::

| Model | NEE | short | long | recurring | 1 day | 1 week | 1 month | 3 months | 1 year |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| short memory | night | 18 h | | | 0.26 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| | day | 2 d | | | 0.56 | 0.02 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| long memory | night | 18 h, 20% | 8 wk, 80% | | 0.84 | 0.71 | 0.47 | 0.16 | 0 |
| | day | 2 d, 42% | 5 wk, 58% | | 0.80 | 0.49 | 0.25 | 0.05 | 0 |
| recurring bias | night | 1 d, 29% | 9 wk, 39% | ±5 wk, 32% | 0.83 | 0.66 | 0.41 | 0.10 | 0.32 |
| | day | 2 d, 48% | 7 wk, 33% | ±2.5 wk, 20% | 0.80 | 0.46 | 0.18 | 0.05 | 0.20 |

: Correlation of the discrepancy at two windows a lag apart

. . .

- **Short memory:** windows a few days apart are nearly independent
- **Long memory:** a misfit lasting a month stays strongly correlated, so is
  cheap
- **Recurring bias:** the same date a year later is correlated again

## LAI, biomass and soil carbon

::: {.corner-note}
Formulas in the appendix
:::

- **LAI:** product's spread (floored) + discrepancy correlated within a
  summer (about a month)
- **Biomass:** satellite error and carbon-fraction error, each shared across
  years, + independent discrepancy
- **Soil carbon:** discrepancy 25% of the stock (a 0–200 cm stock vs one
  model pool)

# Harvard Forest: the prior

## Calibration parameters

::: {.corner-note}
$[l, u]$: the central 95% interval. Independent marginals
:::

| Parameter $(D = 15)$ | Prior |
|---|---|
| photosynthetic capacity $P$ (nmol g⁻¹ s⁻¹) | log-normal, $[140, 450]$ |
| foliar respiration share $\rho$ | logit-normal, $[0.04, 0.20]$ |
| optimum photosynthesis temperature $T_{\text{opt}}$ (°C) | $\mathcal N(22, 2.5^2)$ |
| half-saturation light $I_{1/2}$ (mol m⁻² d⁻¹) | log-normal, $[4.6, 26.3]$ |
| soil water holding capacity $W$ (cm) | log-normal, $[15, 150]$ |
| leaf growth at leaf-on (g C m⁻²) | log-normal, $[50, 180]$ |
| leaf-on growing degree-days (°C d) | log-normal, $[500, 1100]$ |
| allocation: leaf, wood, fine root, coarse root (4, on the simplex) | softmax-normal about $(0.18, 0.45, 0.065, 0.305)$ |
| wood respiration rate at 10 °C (yr⁻¹) | log-normal, $[0.006, 0.04]$ |
| soil respiration flux at 10 °C (g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) | log-normal, $[200, 900]$ |
| soil respiration $Q_{10}$ | log-normal, $[1.3, 3.2]$ |
| initial wood carbon, initial soil carbon (kg C m⁻²) | log-normal, fitted to an initial-condition ensemble |

## Reparameterizing for identifiability

::: {.corner-note}
SIPNET's photosynthesis in the appendix
:::

- Four photosynthesis parameters $A, f, r, c$ enter the model only through
  two combinations:

$$
P = \frac{A\,(f + r)}{c},
\qquad
\rho = \frac{r}{f + r}
$$

. . .

$$
\mathrm{GPP} = P\, C_{\text{leaf}} \times \underbrace{D_T D_{\text{VPD}} D_{\text{light}} D_{\text{water}}}_{\text{stresses in } [0, 1]},
\qquad
R_{\text{leaf}} = \rho\, P\, C_{\text{leaf}} \times \underbrace{Q_{10}^{(T - T_{\text{opt}})/10}}_{\text{temperature}}
$$

. . .

- Calibrate $(P, \rho)$: capacity, and the share the leaves respire
- Fix $f$, $c$; map back to $A$, $r$

## The noise scales

::: {.corner-note}
Shaded: the central 90%, $[0.35, 4.72]$; dashed: the median
:::

$$
s_k^2 \overset{\text{ind}}{\sim} \mathrm{IG}(a_k, b_k),
\qquad a_k = 2,\quad b_k = \operatorname{median}\,\mathrm{Gamma}(2, 1) \approx 1.678
$$

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- Median 1: $\Sigma_k$ is the reference
- Central 90%: the noise standard deviation times 0.59 to 2.2
- **Fixed noise:** $s_k^2 = 1$, the prior median
- **Inferred noise:** $s_k$ unknown
:::

# Inference Algorithms

## Ensemble Kalman inversion: one update

::: {.corner-note}
$J$: ensemble size (100 here)
:::

- Ensemble $\theta^{(1)}, \dots, \theta^{(J)}$; run $g^{(j)} = \mathcal G(\theta^{(j)})$:
  one parallel batch

. . .

- Fit a joint Gaussian to $(\theta, g)$ by the ensemble's moments; condition
  on $y$:

::: {.algorithm-box}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{EKI\text{-}UPDATE}\big(\theta^{(j)} \mid s, \Delta\beta\big)
&= \theta^{(j)} + \hat C_{\theta g}\Big(\hat C_{gg} + \tfrac{\Sigma(s)}{\Delta\beta}\Big)^{-1}\big(y - g^{(j)} - \eta^{(j)}\big), \\
\eta^{(j)} &\sim \mathcal N\Big(0,\ \tfrac{\Sigma(s)}{\Delta\beta}\Big)
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

. . .

- $\Delta\beta = 1$: Gaussian conditioning, $K = \hat C_{\theta g}(\hat C_{gg} + \Sigma)^{-1}$
- Exact for linear $\mathcal G$, Gaussian prior, $J \to \infty$
- No gradients; no likelihood evaluations

## EKI: tempering

$$
\pi_\beta(\theta) \;\propto\; \pi_0(\theta)\; \mathcal N\big(y \mid \mathcal G(\theta),\ \Sigma\big)^{\beta},
\qquad \beta: 0 \to 1
$$

. . .

- An increment $\Delta\beta$ = conditioning with noise inflated to $\Sigma/\Delta\beta$:
  $\ \mathcal N(y \mid \mathcal G, \Sigma)^{\Delta\beta} \propto \mathcal N(y \mid \mathcal G, \Sigma/\Delta\beta)$

. . .

::: {.algorithm-box}
$\theta^{(j)} \sim \pi_0$, $\ \beta = 0$; **while** $\beta < 1$:

1. $\Delta\beta$: adaptive, keeping the ESS of weights $e^{-\Delta\beta\, \Phi_j}$ at $J/2$, $\ \Phi_j = \tfrac12\|y - g^{(j)}\|^2_{\Sigma}$
2. $\theta^{(j)} \leftarrow \mathrm{EKI\text{-}UPDATE}\big(\theta^{(j)} \mid s = 1, \Delta\beta\big)$ $\quad$ (one batch of $J$ runs)
3. $\beta \leftarrow \beta + \Delta\beta$
:::

. . .

- Few stages, each one parallel batch
- An approximation for nonlinear $\mathcal G$, not a consistent sampler

## EKI with unknown noise scales

::: {.corner-note}
After Botha et al. (2023), *Inverse Problems* 39, 125014
:::

$$
\pi_\beta(\theta, s) \;\propto\; \pi_0(\theta)\, p(s)\; \mathcal N\big(y \mid \mathcal G(\theta),\ \Sigma(s)\big)^{\beta}
$$

. . .

Alternate a Kalman step in $\theta$ and a Gibbs step in $s$:

::: {.algorithm-box}
$(\theta^{(j)}, s^{(j)}) \sim \pi_0 \times p$, $\ \beta = 0$; **while** $\beta < 1$:

1. $\Delta\beta$: adaptive, as before
2. $\theta^{(j)} \leftarrow \mathrm{EKI\text{-}UPDATE}\big(\theta^{(j)} \mid s^{(j)}, \Delta\beta\big)$ $\quad$ (one batch of $J$ runs)
3. $s^{(j)} \sim \pi_{\beta + \Delta\beta}\big(s \mid \theta^{(j)}, y\big)$ $\quad$ (conjugate: exact, no runs)
4. $\beta \leftarrow \beta + \Delta\beta$
:::

. . .

- Which $s$ in the gain: one common, or each particle's own (appendix)
- Still approximate: corrected next

## Correcting EKI {.big-table}

::: {.corner-note}
$q$: Student-t ($\nu = 5$, covariance $\times 1.5$) fitted to EKI's
ensemble, mixed 9:1 with the prior
:::

**Target:** $\pi(\theta) \propto \pi_0(\theta)\, L(\theta)$

- Fixed noise: $L(\theta) = \mathcal N\big(y \mid \mathcal G(\theta), \Sigma\big)$, all $s_k = 1$
- Inferred noise: $s$ integrated out, $L(\theta) = \prod_k t_{2a_k}\big(y_k \mid \mathcal G_k(\theta),\ \tfrac{b_k}{a_k} \Sigma_k\big)$;
  $s$ drawn afterwards from its conditional

. . .

**Base density:** $q \approx$ EKI's ensemble, heavy-tailed, mixed with the prior

. . .

| | draws from | corrected by | rounds of runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Importance sampling | $q$ | weights $\pi_0 L / q$ | 1 |
| Tempered SMC | $q^{1-\beta}(\pi_0 L)^{\beta}$, $\ \beta: 0 \to 1$ | reweight, resample, MH moves | stages $\times$ moves |
| MCMC | random-walk Metropolis | accept / reject | one per step |

## Importance sampling and tempered SMC

::: {.corner-note}
Details in the appendix
:::

**Importance sampling**

- $\theta_m \sim q$, $\ \tilde w_m = \pi_0(\theta_m) L(\theta_m) / q(\theta_m)$
- One batch; consistent whatever EKI's bias
- Prior component bounds the weights: $\tilde w \le 10\, L$

. . .

**Tempered SMC**: when the weights degenerate

- Bridge $\pi_\beta \propto q^{1-\beta}(\pi_0 L)^{\beta}$ from $q$ to the target
- Each stage: reweight (adaptive $\Delta\beta$), resample, move by
  Metropolis–Hastings invariant for $\pi_\beta$
- Importance sampling = one stage, no moves

# Appendix

## NEE: measurement error

::: {.corner-note}
AmeriFlux's hourly `RANDUNC` ($r_h$) and `JOINTUNC` ($j_h$). A window
reporting neither takes its source's median
:::

A window $W$ averages 12 hourly values; the tower reports two uncertainties
per hour:

- **Random** $r_h$: independent from hour to hour $\Rightarrow$ averages down
- **Filtering** $u_h = \sqrt{\max(j_h^2 - r_h^2,\ 0)}$: the spread over
  friction-velocity ($u_*$) filtering thresholds; shared by the whole
  window $\Rightarrow$ does not average down

. . .

$$
\operatorname{Var}(e_W)
= \underbrace{\frac{1}{12}\, \operatorname{mean}_{h \in W} r_h^2}_{\text{random: averages down}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\big(\operatorname{mean}_{h \in W} u_h\big)^2}_{\text{filtering: shared}}
$$

- Independent across windows: $\Sigma^{\text{obs}}$ diagonal

## NEE: the error models' kernels {.big-table}

::: {.corner-note}
$t_W$: the window's end, in days. Weights and timescales: maximum-likelihood
fits to an earlier calibration's residuals, used for their shape only
:::

$$
\big(\Sigma^{\delta}_k\big)_{WW'} = v^\delta_k\, \rho^L_k(t_W - t_{W'}),
\qquad
\rho^L_k = \sum_m w_m\, \kappa_m
$$

$$
\kappa_\tau(\Delta) = e^{-|\Delta|/\tau},
\quad
\kappa^{\text{per}}_\lambda(\Delta) = \exp\!\Big(-\frac{2\sin^2(\pi\Delta/P)}{\lambda^2}\Big),
\ P = 365.25
$$

| Error model $L$ | $\rho^L$, night | $\rho^L$, day |
|---|---|---|
| short memory | $\kappa_{0.74}$ | $\kappa_{1.72}$ |
| long memory | $0.20\,\kappa_{0.74} + 0.80\,\kappa_{57.2}$ | $0.42\,\kappa_{1.72} + 0.58\,\kappa_{36.5}$ |
| recurring bias | $0.29\,\kappa_{1.17} + 0.39\,\kappa_{64.2} + 0.32\,\kappa^{\text{per}}_{0.437}$ | $0.48\,\kappa_{1.78} + 0.33\,\kappa_{46.6} + 0.20\,\kappa^{\text{per}}_{0.208}$ |

$v^\delta_k$: $1.43^2$ (night), $2.99^2$ (day), in (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹)², the same
for every $L$

## LAI, biomass and soil carbon: covariances

::: {.corner-note}
$\sigma_i$, $\sigma_j$, $\sigma$: each product's reported standard deviations;
$t_i$ in days
:::

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{LAI:}\quad & (\Sigma_{\text{LAI}})_{ii'} = \max(\sigma_i,\ 0.66)^2\, \mathbf 1[i = i']
  + 0.5^2\, e^{-|t_i - t_{i'}|/30}\, \mathbf 1[\text{same summer}] \\[4pt]
\text{biomass:}\quad & \Sigma_{\text{biomass}} = \sigma\sigma^\top + \kappa^2\, y y^\top + 5^2 I,
  \qquad \kappa = 0.02 / 0.48 \\[4pt]
\text{soil C:}\quad & \Sigma_{\text{soil C}} = \sigma^2 + (0.25\, y)^2
\end{aligned}
$$

## EKI with noise scales: the details

::: {.corner-note}
$q_k(\theta) = \|y_k - \mathcal G_k(\theta)\|^2_{\Sigma_k}$, $\ n_k = \dim y_k$
:::

- **$s$ step**, by conjugacy:
  $\ \pi_\beta(s_k^2 \mid \theta, y) = \mathrm{IG}\big(s_k^2 \mid a_k + \tfrac{\beta n_k}{2},\ b_k + \tfrac{\beta\, q_k(\theta)}{2}\big)$
- **Increment:** the ESS of the ratio of the $s$-marginal tempered targets,

$$
\log w_j = \sum_k \Big[A_k(\beta) \log B_{jk}(\beta) - A_k(\beta') \log B_{jk}(\beta')\Big]
$$

$$
A_k(\beta) = a_k + \tfrac{\beta n_k}{2},
\quad
B_{jk}(\beta) = b_k + \tfrac{\beta\, q_k(\theta^{(j)})}{2}
$$

- **Marginal** in $\theta$:
  $p(y_k \mid \theta) = t_{2a_k}\big(y_k \mid \mathcal G_k(\theta),\ \tfrac{b_k}{a_k} \Sigma_k\big)$

## EKI with noise scales: two $\theta$ steps

::: {.corner-note}
$T, U$: the centered ensembles of $\theta$ and $g$ over $\sqrt{J - 1}$, so
$\hat C_{\theta g} = T^\top U$, $\hat C_{gg} = U^\top U$
:::

- **Common gain:** one scale for every particle, the mean precision
  $\bar s_k^2 = \big(\tfrac1J \sum_j 1/(s^{(j)}_k)^2\big)^{-1}$:
  $\ \mathrm{EKI\text{-}UPDATE}(\theta^{(j)} \mid \bar s, \Delta\beta)$;
  tends to under-disperse
- **Per-particle gain:** each particle's own $s^{(j)}$, with $T, U$ less
  their least-squares fit on $\log s^{(j)}$ (an estimate of
  $\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cov}(\theta, g \mid s)]$); tends to
  over-disperse

. . .

- Neither is exact even for linear $\mathcal G$: the ensemble's covariance is
  the marginal's, which exceeds $\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cov}(\theta \mid s)]$
  by $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbb E[\theta \mid s])$
- The two coincide as $\operatorname{Var}(s \mid y)$ shrinks

## Importance sampling and SMC: the details

$$
q = 0.9\; t_5\big(\hat m,\ 1.5\, \hat C\big) + 0.1\, \pi_0
$$

$$
W_m = \frac{\tilde w_m}{\sum_{m'} \tilde w_{m'}},
\qquad
\mathrm{ESS} = \frac{1}{\sum_m W_m^2},
\qquad
\hat Z = \frac1M \sum_m \tilde w_m
$$

Tempered SMC, $\ell = \log \pi_0 + \log L - \log q$; each stage:

1. **Increment:** the largest $\delta$ with
   $\mathrm{CESS}(\delta) = \dfrac{\big(\sum_i W_i e^{\delta \ell_i}\big)^2}{\sum_i W_i e^{2\delta \ell_i}} \ge \tfrac12$
2. **Reweight:** $W_i \propto W_i\, e^{\delta \ell_i}$;
   $\ \log \hat Z \mathrel{+}= \log \sum_i W_i e^{\delta \ell_i}$
3. **Resample** systematically
4. **Move** by Metropolis–Hastings: an independent $t_5(\hat m, \hat C)$ or a
   random walk $\theta + \lambda \hat L z$, until 99% of the samples have
   moved

## MCMC: the details

$$
\theta_c' = \theta_c + \lambda\, \frac{2.38}{\sqrt D}\, L z_c,
\quad z_c \sim \mathcal N(0, I_D),
\qquad
\text{accepted with probability } \min\Big(1,\ \frac{\pi(\theta_c')}{\pi(\theta_c)}\Big)
$$

- **Start:** $C$ draws resampled by weight from an importance-sampling run;
  $LL^\top$ the covariance of the EKI ensemble behind it; $\lambda = 1$
- **Adapt**, during the first 500 steps: every 25 steps
  $\log \lambda \mathrel{+}= 2(\bar a - 0.234)$, $\bar a$ their acceptance
  rate; from step 100, every 50 steps, $LL^\top$ re-estimated from the second
  half of all chains' history
- **Then freeze** the kernel and discard the first 1000 of 2000 steps

## SIPNET's photosynthesis

::: {.corner-note}
`sipnet.c` at SIPNET v2.2.0-alpha.1. $\omega$: a units constant. Leaf
respiration is also reduced when the soil is frozen
:::

$$
\mathrm{GPP} = \underbrace{A\,(f + r)}_{\text{gross capacity}}\; \frac{C_{\text{leaf}}}{c}\;
D_T\, D_{\text{VPD}}\, D_{\text{light}}\, D_{\text{water}}\; \omega,
\qquad
R_{\text{leaf}} = r A\, \frac{C_{\text{leaf}}}{c}\, \omega\; Q_{10}^{(T - T_{\text{opt}})/10}
$$

- $A$ `aMax`, the maximum rate per gram of leaf, in full light and with no
  stress; $f$ `aMaxFrac`, its daily mean as a fraction; $r$ `baseFolRespFrac`, leaf respiration as a fraction
  of $A$; $c$ `cFracLeaf`, the carbon fraction of leaf mass
- $D_T = \max\!\Big(0,\ \dfrac{(T_{\max} - T)(T - T_{\min})}{\big((T_{\max} - T_{\min})/2\big)^2}\Big)$,
  $\ T_{\max} = 2T_{\text{opt}} - T_{\min}$
- $D_{\text{light}} = \displaystyle\int_0^1 \big(1 - 2^{-I e^{-k\, \mathrm{LAI}\, \ell} / I_{1/2}}\big)\, d\ell$,
  the canopy's mean light response
- $D_{\text{VPD}} \in [0, 1]$ falls with vapor pressure deficit;
  $D_{\text{water}} \in [0, 1]$ is the transpiration the soil water (up to
  $W$) can supply over the demand
